Cc: Primex Engineering <eng@primex.ai>, support@primex.ai
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: spike in 5xx + token latency — urgent

Hi Vivek,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 5xx responses and median token latency at ~09:00 PDT from our Primex-AZ1 footprint. Impact is heavy on our customer-facing inference endpoints (search and chat). Screenshot attached. Our incident runbooks are showing failed retries and bad user experience across several regions pegged to AZ1 routing.

Can Redwood immediately prioritize routing away from AZ1 or place a temporary rate cap? We need a mitigation ASAP — our CS team is getting drowned in tickets.

Thanks,
Samantha Park
Head of Site Reliability
Primex.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Samantha Park <samantha.park@primex.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: spike in 5xx + token latency — urgent

Team — quick tech notes from the run: 
- Root symptoms: abrupt request queue depth increase on AZ1 inference pool (gpt-large family), KV cache pressure, occasional OOM on a subset of instances.
- Correlated indicators: increased token replays observed (~12%), allocation thrash in the 09:01–09:10 window.
- Current health: controller has started soft-throttling new containers; some nodes are flapping 502s but not full host failures.

Mitigation options (fastest → slower):
1) Immediate cross-region steer at the load balancer level (steer ~60–80% of Primex traffic from AZ1 to AZ2/USW2). Pros: immediate customer relief; Cons: risk of capacity bumps in target AZs and model cold-start latency.
2) Prefix caching aggressive policy for Primex (reduce token generation pressure) — library changes needed, ~15–30m to roll.
3) Temporary per-client rate-limiter to cap noisy endpoints (requires Primex consent).

I recommend option 1 now with careful throttling and monitoring, then option 2 as a follow-up. If we go with option 1 we need an exec-authorized temporary priority for Primex routing and a containment communications plan.

Attaching a proposed playbook: proposed-steer-playbook-v2.pdf
— Hannah
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- proposed-steer-playbook-v2.pdf (application/pdf stub)

Marissa / Vivek — short commercial impact note for execs: Primex is public-facing retail search; outage is user-visible (checkout search slow/failing). We estimate ~0.8–1.1% revenue leakage if this persists >30m. Primex is an annual committed customer on Dedicated with a mid-tier SLA.

If we propose redirected priority lanes or emergency credits, we should quantify: 1) one-time credit (X% of last month spend), 2) temporary priority capacity access (2x baseline for 2 hours), 3) commit to a post-incident technical remediation plan.

I can draft the short memo for Marissa’s sign-off. Need to know whether the SRE recommended steer is the approved tactical.

— Ben
Head of Support Escalations
Redwood Inference

Team — thanks for the rapid triage. Vivek — please present the ask succinctly; I’ll escalate to CEO and Ops execs for immediate authorization if needed. Two decision points we need answered in the next 20 minutes:
1) Technical: Confirm planned steer percentage, expected failover latency increase, and target AZs’ spare capacity margin. Hannah — can you confirm numbers?
2) Commercial: If steer triggers >X traffic onto dedicated pools and we need to reallocate priority capacity, what is the recommended interim commercial concession? Ben — suggest a one-line credit proposal.

If both answers are green, I will approve the steer and overnight commit to the temporary capacity reallocation. Also cc’ing Rachel to prep the customer comms.

Onwards.
— Marissa Cole
SVP, Customer Operations

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Samantha Park <samantha.park@primex.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Aug 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: spike in 5xx + token latency — urgent

Decision summary (for Marissa / execs):
- Technical ask (approve now): Perform a controlled cross-region steer routing 70% of Primex AZ1 traffic to AZ2 & USW2 (50%→AZ2, 20%→USW2). Expected user-visible median response bump ~80–120ms for affected calls; projected immediate reduction of 5xx from ~3.5% → <0.3% within 3–6 minutes. Target AZs have ~30% spare serving headroom by current telemetry. Hannah will run the steer in gradual phases (10% increments every 90s) and monitor KVs + cold-starts.

- Commercial ask (authorize if you approve steer): Grant Primex a one-time credit equal to 10% of their July invoice (to offset user impact and goodwill). Additionally offer an incident root-cause technical review within 7 business days and a prioritized follow-up for model-quantization suggestions.

Proposed comms cadence after approval: 1) immediate acknowledgement email from Vivek with mitigation note; 2) 30-minute technical update; 3) post-incident RCA + remediation plan.

Marissa — please confirm OK to proceed. If green I will kick off the steer and the customer comms.

— Vivek
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
